title: AstraGrid Energy compliance readout & evidence access planning
summary: Redwood presented current SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, discussed trust center access model, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit log retention, and encryption/KMS integration options. Customer requested gated access to reports, a controls mapping spreadsheet, and a technical deep dive on KMS/HSM and data residency implications for EU customers.
topics: Data residency and EU region controls
next_steps: Redwood to share redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO statement via secure link (Redwood)
Schedule KMS technical deep dive with SEs and Lina (Joint)
Provide controls mapping spreadsheet for AstraGrid workloads (Redwood)
Create Trust Center read-only accounts for Ellen and Ravi (Redwood)
Follow up on legal NDA scope for full SOC 2 report delivery (Legal teams)

Diego Morales (Redwood SE) - prepare KMS/HSM integration deck and proposed architecture by 2025-12-09

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~54 minutes | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CS); Ellen (AstraGrid - Head of Compliance), Ravi (Security Lead), Lina (Cloud Architect), Marco (Legal).

[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Ellen: Hi Ellen here, I'll lead from AstraGrid.
[00:10] Ravi: Ravi on security.
[00:12] Lina: Lina, cloud.
[00:15] Marco: Marco, legal.
[00:18] Samira: Great. Purpose today is a compliance readout and to plan how we get evidence and trust center access — high level SOC 2/ISO posture and the mechanics for you to validate controls. Diego will jump into the technical bits.
[00:33] Diego: Thanks Samira. Quick note on cert status: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II covering our hosted inference control environment through 2025-09-30 for the last review period, and an ISO 27001 certificate current as of Q2 2025, we can share the statements.
[00:50] Marco: Are those the full reports or just the attestation letter? Legal needs to see scope and any subservice orgs.
[00:58] Samira: We typically share a redacted full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; attestation plus control narratives. Full PII-sensitive pages are redacted. We can provide scope details and subservice org listings in the controls mapping spreadsheet.
[01:15] Ellen: For our auditors we need the control mappings to our control IDs, and any evidence links. How do customers access those artifacts?
[01:24] Priya: We use a Trust Center portal — secure, SSO-bound accounts. Customers get role-based access (read-only for compliance, admin for operational teams).
[01:34] Lina: Does that support SCIM group sync or just manual invites? We want automatic group sync from Okta to avoid admin overhead.
[01:40] Diego: We support SAML SSO today and have SCIM provisioning for groups in beta; we can enable SCIM for enterprise customers on dedicated/private deployments. For hosted customers we now offer SAML + manual group role mapping; SCIM rollout for hosted is planned and we can show roadmap and timeline in the next doc.
[02:05] Ravi: Audit logs are another big one. What's retention and can we export logs to our SIEM?
[02:11] Diego: Audit logging: we retain admin and API logs for 90 days by default in the hosted plan, longer retention available as an add-on — exports to S3 or a push into your SIEM (via secured delivery) are supported. For Dedicated/Private deployments you control retention and can ship logs directly to your logging stack.
[02:34] Ravi: For our EU customers we need to guarantee data residency for tokens and logs, at least for persisted artifacts. How is that handled?
[02:42] Samira: We offer region pinning — requests, KV cache, and persisted artifacts can be constrained to EU regions on Dedicated or Private. Hosted customers can elect EU-only hosting; we can show the cert mappings and where attestations apply.
[03:01] Ellen: On encryption, do you use customer-managed keys? HSM-backed? We have strict controls requiring CMK for production models that process regulated data.
[03:10] Diego: Yes. We support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys. For Dedicated and Private you can integrate with your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM via KMIP). We can outline envelope encryption and key rotation processes.
[03:28] Marco: From a legal perspective, if we get the redacted SOC 2 will that satisfy our T&Cs or do we need an additional Data Processing Addendum?
[03:35] Samira: Most customers sign DPA plus the standard SOW; we'll include the DPA template. If there are special clauses we can route through legal.
[03:44] Lina: Can you map specific Redwood controls to our control IDs? For example, how does your access control map to our control ACC-03?
[03:52] Diego: Absolutely. We'll provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that includes Redwood control reference, control narrative, evidence artifacts, and suggested cross-reference to customer control IDs. We'll ask you to share a list of priority control IDs.
[04:10] Ellen: Ok, timeline: we need the mapping and either a read-only Trust Center account or the full redacted reports for our internal auditors in two weeks. Is that feasible?
[04:19] Samira: Yes — redacted SOC 2 + ISO statement via secure link within 48-72 hours after NDA confirmation; controls mapping spreadsheet within 5 business days; Trust Center accounts provisioned within 2-3 business days once we have login emails.
[04:33] Ravi: What about endpoint security and supply chain? Do you publish SBOMs or vendor lists?
[04:40] Diego: We publish our third-party vendor list in the Trust Center and summarize vendor risk treatment. SBOMs are available for our runtime components on request under an NDA for customers with higher assurance needs.
[04:56] Marco: We will coordinate NDA scope with legal then. Also need clarity on subprocessor list and subprocess modes for private deployments.
[05:05] Priya: We'll include subprocessor list and the subprocess controls in the package.
[05:12] Ellen: On evidence access - can we lock down view-only to specific IP ranges? We have strict controls around where compliance reviewers can log in from.
[05:20] Diego: We can enforce IP allowlists on Trust Center access for enterprise accounts and SSO session policies. For hosted accounts we can enable IP restrictions per account. For Private deployments, obviously, you control the network.
[05:36] Lina: For the KMS integration deep dive — can the Redwood runtime call out to our KMS for on-the-fly decryption of model weights or only for token-level envelope keys? We're designing a workflow that avoids exposing keys to runtime.
[05:48] Diego: Current pattern is envelope encryption: model artifacts are encrypted at rest with a CMK; runtime fetches encrypted segments and decrypts using a short-lived data key derived via KMS; keys are never persisted in plaintext. For full on-prem HSM pass-through there's an architecture we can walk through in the tech deep dive.
[06:07] Ellen: That architecture detail is critical. Also, does SOC 2 cover your Dedicated offering or only hosted?
[06:13] Samira: Our SOC 2 coverage includes the control environment for hosted and our managed dedicated control processes; for Private (customer-managed), the certificate covers the control processes we operate, but customer infrastructure elements are out of scope — we'll document the boundaries clearly.
[06:30] Marco: Are penetration test results included anywhere?
[06:34] Diego: High-level pen test summaries are in Trust Center; detailed reports are available under NDA. We'll include a summary and dates.
[06:44] Ravi: On audit logs again — do you provide immutable logs or tamper-evident storage for audit trails?
[06:50] Diego: Logs are stored with write-once semantics in our logging pipeline and we can export to append-only S3 buckets or to your SIEM with immutability settings. For Private deployments you can choose WORM buckets.
[07:06] Ellen: Ok if we get the spreadsheet and the redacted reports we can start uploading to our internal auditor portal. Next, technical deep dive — who should attend from Redwood?
[07:15] Samira: Diego and one of our infra engineers — I'll include Priya for compliance handoff. How about the week of Dec 8?
[07:22] Lina: That's good. Preferred timezone mornings PST.
[07:26] Samira: Noted.
[07:28] Marco: One more legal Q — retention of logs and data after contract termination. Do you have a documented purge process?
[07:35] Diego: Yes, documented retention and secure deletion processes — we can share the runbook and certificate of deletion for terminated customers.
[07:45] Ellen: Are there any outstanding gaps you see in our ask compared to Redwood's default config?
[07:51] Diego: From this call the main items are: 1) SCIM provisioning for group sync (not yet GA for hosted), 2) extended audit log retention for hosted without add-on, 3) mapping to your control IDs which we'll deliver via spreadsheet. None are blockers.
[08:12] Ravi: For the timeline on extended retention — what's the cost model?
[08:17] Samira: We have a pricing add-on for log retention and a usage-based export bandwidth cost. We'll include a pricing line in the follow-up.
[08:27] Ellen: Ok let's recap next steps.
[08:30] Samira: Recap: Redwood will (1) send redacted SOC 2 and ISO statement via secure SSO-protected link after NDA; (2) provision Trust Center read-only accounts for Ellen and Ravi; (3) deliver controls mapping spreadsheet; (4) schedule KMS/HSM deep dive with Diego and infra; (5) include subprocessor list, pen test summary and retention runbook. Any additions?
[08:56] Marco: We'll finalize NDA scope and return to you within two business days.
[09:02] Lina: I'll send the priority control IDs and our auditor contact by EOD Dec 5.
[09:08] Samira: Great. I'll follow up with calendar invites and a secure link. Thanks everyone.
[09:14] Ellen: Thanks all.
[09:16] End of call.

Notes: transcription contains minor inaccuracies; speaker attributions reconciled post-call by AE. Links referenced during call: Trust Center link (sent in follow-up), controls mapping template (to be shared), redacted SOC 2 via secure link (upon NDA).
